I've been thinking about this a lot lately. Lots of people think the mainstream media is dishonest, clickbaity, or just generally bad. However, for years and years they have been driving presidential races. Is it possible that we've been pushed to worry about things that aren't really important because the media outlets know that sensationalizing certain stories will allow a constant stream of similar controversies in the future?

Regardless of whether the above is worthwhile speculation or tinfoil-hat craziness, I want to know what criteria you guys use when deciding who to support.

Eloquence? Presidents will need to be able to speak in front of the whole nation, and for the whole nation. On the flip side, in politics, eloquence tends to come with guarded, scripted language that may be more of the "politics as usual" people are getting upset with. Maybe Bernie being willing to say "people are tired of your damn emails" and Trump being... Trump... aren't such bad qualities.

Credentials? And if so, what kind of credentials? Would a former governor be better than a senator because of executive experience? What about a former prosecutor like fatass Christie? Or a CEO like Fiorina? Do these things matter for you?

Issues Do the presidents stances hold a majority of the weight for you? I question this one a lot, because the obvious counter is that in our system of gvt the president doesn't always get their way. If a president disagrees with you on things like abortion, where the supreme court has ruled, does that really matter? Does a candidates stance on regulation matter more than their tax plan because they have more direct control over agencies than Congress?

"Likability" Or, as I've been telling my friends recently, do you just want a candidate you wouldn't mind seeing on TV and having to listen to for 4 years? I kind of feel this way. There are certainly candidates I'd get sick of, and some who I think would be entertaining, or at least tolerable.

Track Record Does having the same stances for many years matter to you? Or do you have a high tolerance for "flip-flopping" provided they seemed to do it for good reason rather than going with what's popular? Maybe flexibility is more important than being rigid.

Gaffes Does having bad sound clips of a candidate saying stupid or incorrect things matter to you?

Please feel free to discuss what I've put up or anything else that comes to mind. I'd really like to hear Voat's thoughts.
